terms.definition: A horizontal row of the periodic table whose elements share the same number of electron shells.
terms.function: Organizes elements by shell count and traces the shift from metals to nonmetals across the row.
terms.whereItIs: The glowing horizontal row of tiles in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Together with groups, periods let you locate any element and predict its basic character.

terms.definition: A layer of space around the nucleus where electrons live.
terms.function: Gives each atom its period — the number of shells matches the row number.
terms.whereItIs: The small shell icons beside each row tile.
terms.whyItMatters: The shell count is the one trait a whole period shares.

terms.definition: An element on the left side of the periodic table — shiny, malleable, and a good conductor of heat and electricity.
terms.function: Behaves as a typical metal; found at the left end of each period.
terms.whereItIs: The warm-toned tiles at the left of the highlighted row.
terms.whyItMatters: Metals dominate the table and every period begins with them.

terms.definition: An element on the right side of the periodic table — generally a poor conductor and often a gas or brittle solid.
terms.function: Behaves very differently from metals; found at the right end of each period.
terms.whereItIs: The cool-toned tiles at the right of the highlighted row.
terms.whyItMatters: The sweep from metal to nonmetal is the most visible pattern across every period.
